exposure: 22 weeks of gestation vs. 23 weeks of gestation
outcome: maternal interventions (cesarean delivery, maternal hospital transfer, or antenatal corticosteroid administration)
neonatal interventions (neonatal intensive care unit admission, surfactant administration, antibiotic administration, or assisted ventilation)
combined interventions (at least one maternal and at least one neonatal intervention)
cohort: U.S. live births at 22 0/7-23 6/7 weeks of gestation from 2012 to 2016
finding: Maternal and neonatal interventions occur frequently at the threshold of viability, especially at 23 weeks of gestation where the occurrence of interventions exceeds 50%.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was one of the maternal interventions analyzed in this study, and it was found that preeclampsia was the factor most positively associated with interventions, while the presence of birth defects was positively associated with maternal interventions.
